questions.answer: Books, if that counts. I find it hard to give any away, so my collection just keeps growing. There's something comforting about a shelf full of books you've read, or still [[intend]] to read one day.

questions.q: Did you collect anything as a child?
questions.answer: Stamps and coins, like lots of children back then. My father would sometimes bring home old coins that customers had given him at the shop, and I kept them in a tin box as if they were [[priceless]] treasures.

questions.q: What kinds of things do people in your country collect?
questions.answer: Stamps and coins used to be the classic choices, though they're less common now. These days younger people are more likely to collect cricket [[memorabilia]], like signed bats or team jerseys, which says a lot about how much the sport means here.

questions.q: Why do you think people like collecting things?
questions.answer: I think it gives people a sense of purpose and achievement, slowly building something over time. There's also the [[thrill of the hunt]], that excitement of finally finding the one missing piece you've been searching for.

questions.q: Would you like to start a new collection in the future?
questions.answer: Maybe, if I ever get to study abroad. I'd love to collect something small from every city I visit, nothing expensive, just a modest [[memento]] that brings the experience back whenever I look at it.
